rules.statement: A conviction for an offense requiring damage or harm as a consequence of deceit cannot be sustained where the damage is too remote and not a necessary consequence of the deceit.
rules.supporting_quote: that the possibilities contemplated by the lower Courts were too remote; that the facts did not constitute an offence under the section; and that the conviction must therefore be set aside." At page 609 it is stated in the judgment that it is clear that the petitioners deceived the Registrar and it is clear that they thereby induced him to register the fictitious deed of divorce- a thing he would not have done unless he had been so deceived. The judgement then goes on to 174 state that in the opinion of the court this act of registering the factitious deed did not cause nor was it likely to cause damage or harm to the Registrar in body, mind, reputation or property. It is also stated in the judgment that the damage or harm must be the necessary consequence of the act done by reason of th deceit practiced or must be necessarily likely to follow therefrom. The possibilities contemplated by the magistrate namely that the registrar suffers not only in registration , but also by losing his fees in future through people declining to avail themselves of his offices , were too remote to be within the contemplation of the statue . The conviction was therefore set aside. In my opinion it is not possible to distinguish the facts in the present case from those in Mojey v. Queen Empress (Supra).
